label: copy-phase input x (from 3rd copied token onward)
explanation: Token detector for the letter x fed back as input during the copy phase. All activation mass is in the copy phase and nearly all of it (>99.9%) is on steps where the input is x; there are essentially none on x during the original phase, on <DEL>, or on other tokens (a few tiny activations on 1/v/n). It needs recall_idx >= 2, i.e. it is silent when x is the first fed-back copy token (recall_idx 1). The firing rate on copy-phase x rises from recall_idx 2 to 3+ and with longer L. Magnitude is largest when x follows e and/or v is being output next (x preceded by e: ~99% precision; out_tok v: ~98% precision; both appear in the top examples). Of qualifying x steps, ~21% stay silent, mostly in short sequences or at the last steps.

issues: All factual claims check out on dev. 100% of activation mass is in the copy phase, with none in the original or delimiter phases. in_tok x carries essentially all the mass, apart from tiny activations on 1 (71 steps), v (12) and n (4). recall_idx 1 has only 6 active steps. x after e scores 0.986 precision and out_tok==v scores 0.980. Test scores (P 0.785, R 0.999) match the reported ones. Missed activations hold 0.0% of the mass.

Wording: the explanation says the 98% holds when 'the next output is v', but that only holds for out_tok==v (0.980), the token output at the x step itself. With next_out==v (the output one step later) precision is 0.917.

Label is slightly off. Firing starts at recall_idx 2, where the fed-back input is original token 1, i.e. the 2nd fed-back token (or the step that outputs the 3rd token). 'From 3rd copied token onward' could be read as recall_idx >= 3, which is a stricter rule than the predicate.

False positives (about 21%) follow a smooth gradient, not a distinct class. Precision is 0.54 at recall_idx 2, 0.80 at recall_idx 3 and 0.88 at recall_idx >= 4, and only 0.49 for L <= 4. Excluding these regions did not beat the original: excluding L<=4 gave dev F1 0.876, excluding (recall_idx 2 & L<=5) gave 0.870 and the recall_idx>=3|L>=8 variant gave 0.865, against 0.880 for the original. So no better crisp predicate exists. The silent steps are graded weak firing early in the copy phase and in short sequences.
